item.title: Houston Texans' C.J. Stroud to be a guest on Monday Night Football's Bengals-Commanders ManningCast
item.description: Houston Texans quarterback C.J. Stroud (7) is seen during the second half of an NFL football game in Houston, Thursday, Nov. 19, 2026. (Jason Fochtman/Houston Chronicle) It's been 13 months since the Houston Texans last played a game on Monday Night Football, but C.J. Stroud will play a small role in Monday night's broadcast of the Cincinnati Bengals-Washington Commanders game this week. The Texans quarterback will be a guest on the ManningCast of Monday night's game, joining hosts Peyton and Eli Manning on ESPN2's broadcast of the game. Former Commanders quarterback Alex Smith also will be a guest on the show. The game will be broadcast on ESPN with the traditional crew of Joe Buck and Troy Aikman, but the Mannings on ESPN2 offer a little something different with their own insights into the game as well as a few guests who join remotely. Stroud will be just this season's third active player to appear on The ManningCast, which does 10 regular season Monday night games a year. Previously, Panthers quarterback Bryce Young and Broncos quarterback Bo Nix have been on as guests. There is a ManningCast scheduled for the Texans' lone Monday night appearance this season when they play at Green Bay on Jan. 4. Stroud is having the best season of his four-year career. The 25-year-old has thrown 22 touchdowns - one off the career-high he set as a rookie - to go along with just four interceptions. His 73 QBR - the best of his career - ranks fifth in the league behind only the 49ers' Brock Purdy (84.6), Bengals' Joe Burrow (81.6), Cowboys' Dak Prescott (80.9) and Patriots' Drake Maye (73.8) Subscribe There’s more to Houston with the Chronicle. item.title: Ex-Chelsea star defends Cole Palmer after criticism over reaction to Leeds loss
item.description: Former Chelsea striker Jimmy Floyd Hasselbaink has defended Cole Palmer ’s commitment after the forward faced scrutiny following Saturday’s 4-1 thrashing at home against Leeds. Palmer failed to score once again, leaving him with just a single goal across his last nine Premier League appearances during a difficult run for Xabi Alonso ’s side. The England outcast attracted attention after the defeat due to an apparent exchange of words with injured team-mate Joao Pedro near the dugout, while reports suggested the Chelsea playmaker did not acknowledge the frustrated home support at Stamford Bridge . However, Hasselbaink told talkSPORT : "No, I don’t think there is discontent. I think there is a frustration that things are not going the way they want to go and certain individuals deal with that better than others. Jimmy Floyd Hasselbaink has defended Palmer (John Walton/PA) (PA Wire) "The expectation is a lot higher than what is being delivered at the minute and that’s from in the camp, but also from outside the camp and let’s not talk about the commitment of Cole Palmer. I don’t think that is the problem. "At the moment you see he is playing different because he is looking for the ball, but looking for the ball way deeper when he should get it way higher. "It’s the midfielders that should find him in a higher position and at the moment the majority of the time he is starting the majority of the play, so he is not playing as high and as much around the box." Following Palmer’s high-profile omission from Thomas Tuchel ’s England squad for the summer World Cup, the 24-year-old launched the new campaign with goals in victories over Fulham and Brighton to help Alonso make a bright start in west London. Palmer’s form has dipped since, however, during a spell in which Tuchel admitted the Chelsea attacker "misses too many opportunities to impress" to earn an international recall. Pressure is building on Xabi Alonso (PA) Alonso and Palmer are both under pressure following a painful first home loss to Leeds in 27 years, which leaves them with five defeats from 11 league fixtures, though Hasselbaink laid the blame on the team as a whole. "When a new manager comes in and especially with the pedigree of Xabi, yeah you think he would make straight away an impact or a big impact but the players are still the same," Hasselbaink said. "Managers do need time to assess things and adjust things, but the same problems keep on occurring at the moment and that’s really the disappointment."

item.title: ‘Tyreek Hill’s back’ – Kansas City Chiefs breakout star reminds me of former wide receiver, says Mike Florio
item.description: Photo by Kevin C. Cox/Getty Images The Kansas City Chiefs’ offense has stepped up a level over the past two weeks, with Patrick Mahomes throwing eight touchdown passes. The running game has also had a different look, rookie Emmett Johnson has stepped into the backfield with Kenneth Walker dealing with an injury. Johnson had 105 rushing yards in Week 11 and one touchdown, plus a further 38 receiving yards from four targets. The rookie wears the Chiefs’ number 10 jersey once worn by wide receiver Tyreek Hill, and Mike Florio sees similarities with his burst of pace. Speaking to Pro Football Talk, Florio explained: “You’ve got to use him. I mean, people see that number 10, and I’ve heard people say it’s Isiah Pacheco. “When I see him running in the open field, I’m thinking Tyreek Hill’s back, it is just the weirdest thing to see. “But he is extremely effective, and there are teams out there kicking themselves that they didn’t draft him when they could.” How Johnson’s 40 yard dash compares to Tyreek Hill Tyreek Hill was also a fifth-round draft pick for the Kansas City Chiefs, 10 years earlier. He went on to win one Super Bowl with Patrick Mahomes, before forcing an exit to sign with the Miami Dolphins. Hill, 32, is attempting to recover from a serious knee injury and wants to revive his NFL career. He was renowned as the fastest player in the NFL, and Florio’s comparison is a major compliment for Emmett Johnson and his own ability to run into space with the ball. Tyreek Hill did not participate at the NFL Combine, but set a 4.29 time at the 40-yard dash at his West Alabama Pro Day. Emmett Johnson’s dash time was an unimpressive 4.56 seconds, which also helps to explain why he fell to the fifth round. The Chiefs still saw something special in him, and Johnson is proving it on the field where it really matters. item.title: “I just want to help the team as much as I can” – Rio Ngumoha reacts to Liverpool’s win over Manchester United
item.description: “I just want to help the team as much as I can” – Rio Ngumoha reacts to Liverpool’s win over Manchester United Rio Ngumoha shines in Liverpool 4-0 win over Manchester United Rio Ngumoha announced himself on one of English football’s biggest stages with a display of composure, incision and end product as Liverpool swept Manchester United aside 4-0 at Anfield. The teenager played a decisive role in a result that quickly took shape after Leny Yoro’s early dismissal. Dominik Szoboszlai opened the scoring from the resulting free-kick, Florian Wirtz doubled the lead after excellent work from Ngumoha, and the young forward then capped his afternoon with a goal of his own before Victor Munoz added the fourth late on. For Liverpool, the scoreline reflected control as much as quality. For Ngumoha, it was a significant afternoon in his development, delivering a goal and an assist in a fixture that carries weight regardless of the circumstances. Rio Ngumoha delivers on biggest stage There was an assurance to Ngumoha’s performance that stood out from the outset. Liverpool had prepared during the week without complete clarity over what to expect from United under a new manager, so there was an element of adaptation required in the opening exchanges. Once Yoro saw red, the contest changed, but the task still demanded patience and precision. Ngumoha handled both. His creative contribution for Wirtz’s finish was one of the afternoon’s standout moments, full of awareness and confidence, and his own goal underlined a willingness to attack decisive spaces. That combination of invention and directness gave Liverpool an edge throughout. His post-match message was measured and team-focused, “I just want to help the team as much as I can”, a line that neatly summed up both the maturity of his outlook and the way he approached the game itself. There was further significance in the numbers. Ngumoha became the second-youngest Liverpool player to score and assist in a Premier League match, after Michael Owen, an indicator of the company he has joined, even if the immediate focus inside the camp will remain on performance levels rather than milestones. item.title: 'My football hasn't changed' - Kevin De Bruyne responds to prospect of Man City being stripped of titles as Napoli star returns to the Etihad
item.description: FBL-EUR-C1-NAPOLI-PRESSER - AFP Kevin De Bruyne insists the prospect of Manchester City being stripped of titles would not change how he views his decade at the Etihad Stadium. Back in Manchester with Napoli, the Belgian declared his love for City's owners and admitted "everybody plays on the limit" of the rules, as he prepares to face his former club in the Champions League on Tuesday. De Bruyne responds to title-stripping threat De Bruyne has insisted his achievements with City will not be tarnished if the club are stripped of titles following the Premier League's guilty verdict. City were found guilty in September of the majority of the financial charges against them, and are appealing the decision. Speaking at a press conference at the Etihad on Monday night, De Bruyne was asked about the possibility of losing honours such as the 100-point title of 2017-18. "It still doesn't change, my football hasn't changed. Of course, in life, there are rules but everybody plays on the limit, I'd say," he said. 'I've given my all' The midfielder, who won six Premier League titles during his 10 years at City, insisted that his legacy is secure. "I've given my all, that's not going to change in my mind, I don't think a lot of people would change in their mind how they view me as a player or how we played," he said. "But... Ah! Everybody has their own opinion, I guess, and how people [say] 'disgrace', I can't change anything about that." De Bruyne added that his relationships with team-mates were what he valued most. 'This is my club! I love the owners' The Belgian made it clear that his bond with City remains as strong as ever, despite the verdict. "And honestly I still... This is my club! I love the owners, I've talked about a lot of stuff outside of football, I've even spoken to Khaldoon [Al Mubarak] how to buy a club and everything," he said. "I've nothing but affection for this club and that will never change! Even now, the people who treated me for 10 years exceptionally, my family and everything, that's for me the most important and for me, that is it to be honest." Emotional Etihad return awaits De Bruyne will now face his old club on Tuesday, as Enzo Maresca's side look to end their slump . The 35-year-old also hit out at reports in the Italian press about his future, saying the coverage had led to unpleasant reactions towards his wife.

item.title: Hero Kanu injury update: Texas football DT could return this year, per Steve Sarkisian
item.description: Texas Longhorns defensive tackle Hero Kanu (93) leads the defense onto the field to warm up ahead of the Red River Rivalry game against the Oklahoma Sooners in Dallas, Oct. 10, 2026. (Sara Diggins/Austin American-Statesman) Texas football 's defensive leader is down, but he might not be out for the rest of the 2026 season, according to Steve Sarkisian . The Longhorns head coach said Monday defensive tackle Hero Kanu could "potentially" return to the field during the College Football Playoff . Kanu tore his biceps in Texas' win at Missouri on Nov. 7. He then tried to play the following week in Texas' win at LSU but was unable to take the field; Kanu underwent surgery last Monday. Sarkisian said last week he expected Kanu to miss the rest of 2026. That timetable has now changed, with at least some chance that Texas gets its man in the middle back on the field this winter. PLAYOFF PUSH: Texas pounds Arkansas in home finale. Will the Longhorns play again in Austin this year? FAMOUS FACES: James Talarico fires cannon at today's game, Gov. Abbott attends, too Kanu, 22, is a fifth-year defensive tackle. The Geltendorf, Germany native recorded 26 tackles, four tackles for loss and a half-sack in nine games this season, though he's continued to make an impact for the Longhorns since injuring his biceps. Sarkisian commended Kanu for his constant chatter both in the locker room and on the sidelines, where a college-football veteran shares both encouragement and tricks of the trade. Kanu has also add another important job since his injury: designated snack delivery man. Defensive end Lance Jackson commended Kanu's sideline skills Monday. "Hero's got you going on the sidelines, hyping you up," Jackson said. "Handing out snacks on the sideline, he's got the Gushers, things of that nature. Hero's a good leader, he keeps you going." Texas Longhorns defensive tackle Hero Kanu (93) says hello to fans as he walks into the stadium ahead of the game between the Texas Longhorns and Florida Gators, Oct. 17, 2026. (Sara Diggins/Austin American-Statesman) Kanu will remain sidelined for Friday's game at Texas A&M as well as Texas' potential appearance in the SEC championship on Saturday, Dec. 5. The Longhorns could play in their first College Football Playoff game as early as Dec. 18, and the CFP will end in the national championship on Jan. 25. The 2025 Challenge Cup winners reached their third straight title game by beating both the Portland Thorns and the Utah Royals in the playoffs, guided by head coach Adrián González, who first joined the club as their interim boss in January 2024. item.title: Colts’ Shane Steichen denies shutting down Alec Pierce for season with heel injury
item.description: Credit: Thomas Shea-Imagn Images Colts’ Shane Steichen denies shutting down Alec Pierce for season with heel injury appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Indianapolis Colts have not ruled out Alec Pierce for the remainder of the 2026 season, despite reports suggesting the wide receiver could be done for the year . Head coach Shane Steichen addressed Pierce’s status and pushed back on those reports , making it clear that the team has not made a decision about shutting him down. “I know there’s reports out there on Alec Pierce being done for the season. We have not made that determination,” Steichen said, via ESPN’s Stephen Holder. “He’s still going through his rehab process. The only way we’ll put him out there is if he’s 100%. We gotta be really smart.” Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Pierce has been sidelined since aggravating his surgically repaired left heel during the Colts’ Week 2 loss to the Kansas City Chiefs. Indianapolis placed him on injured reserve in September, and he has yet to establish a timeline for his return. The fifth-year receiver underwent surgery on the same heel and ankle during the offseason before returning for the start of the regular season. Unfortunately, the injury resurfaced just two games into the year, leaving the Colts without one of their top receiving options. While Steichen has not ruled out a return, his comments make it clear that Indianapolis will not rush Pierce back onto the field . The Colts want him fully healthy before considering a return, and there is no guarantee that happens before the end of the season. For now, Pierce remains in the rehab process, and the Colts are leaving the door open for a possible return. item.title: Hawkeyes Football Depth Chart: Week 13 Iowa vs Nebraska
item.description: The University of Iowa Athletics Department has officially released its Week 13 depth chart as the Hawkeyes prepare to honor their seniors at home one last time. Friday’s game is officially sold out. Besides honoring the seniors, Friday is also the 16 th annual Heros Game. Citizen heroes are honored from each state, and UI Athletics has selected Hannah Jorgensen as Iowa’s hero. Hannah, 24, a fifth-grade teacher at Borlaug Elementary School in Coralville, was on a class field trip to the MacBride Nature Recreation Area when a student slipped and fell into the water. Hannah dove into the lake to rescue the student, and unfortunately both lost their lives. At strong safety, Anthony Hawkins is listed as the starter, after Xavier Styles missed last Saturday’s game against Illinois. First year player Marcello Vitti is listed as the backup. Tony Diaz is still listed on the depth chart as the starter. Diaz had been battling soft tissue issues last week (most likely a hamstring), but in Saturday’s game he logged 67 of Iowa’s 78 offensive snaps and was their leading receiver with four catches for 52 yards and added two carries for 21 yards. Center Cael Winter is listed as the starter after he was cleared to return to the lineup last week after he had missed the last two games and played all 78 offensive snaps. Zach Lutmer remains as the listed starter. Lutmer had initially been listed as questionable on the initial injury report last week but then was cleared to play. Lutmer played 58 defensive snaps, tying Anthony Hawkins and Deshaun Lee for the highest snap total in Iowa’s secondary, and finished with five tackles No changes to special teams. item.title: OVC instruction guide three weeks into the season
item.description: The Ohio Valley Conference is 6-37 against DI opponents this season, entering the start of Feast Week…not exactly the ideal way the conference expected to enter the season, especially when 11 of those losses have been by 10 points or fewer. It’s rough going for a conference that many thought was underrated entering the season, but there are some bright spots in this deep, dark valley up to this point. UT Martin: Heart attack warning The Skyhawks are legitimately three possessions away from 7-0, yet they sit at a respectable 4-3 headed into the final night of the U.S. Virgin Islands Paradise Jam. After seven games of Jeremy Shulman’s team, it is very clear that this is the best team in the OVC. Even though there are plenty of things that need to be polished up before conference play begins, UT Martin boasts wins over Arkansas State and Southern Illinois, with close losses at Tulane, IU Indy, and against Utah Valley, all powered by the star backcourt of Davi Remagen and Kaan Onat. While almost completely different physically, with Remagen relying on his speed and athleticism to blow by defenders and get shots up quickly, and Onat using his strength to methodically break down defenses, the duo have immediately made their names on the national scene. Sasha Savkov as well has been a very important part of their success, using his 6-foot-11 frame and shooting ability to send his team on big runs when needed. Western Illinois: Some assembly required The Leathernecks have opened their season with four losses by eight or fewer points to DI opponents, but a big win over Canisius on Sunday, along with an impressive showing at the Queen City Classic overall, has really proven that Chad Boudreau’s team has some high-level potential if its pieces can fit together. Daivion Traylor has been fantastic through five games, averaging 14.4 points and 7.3 rebounds per outing, and sophomore returner Makai Kvamme has been the quality guard that Boudreau has been looking for, averaging 10.4 points and almost two steals per game. The perimeter defense has been the biggest strength, with WIU forcing teams to a conference-low 25.5% from beyond the arc. Unfortunately, teams are finding ways around that, with the interior defense sitting in the bottom 30 in DI (60.1%FG on two-pointers) While the offense is still truly a work in progress, Western Illinois has the pieces to put themselves in the same position they were in during Boudreau’s first year at the helm just three years ago, when the Leathernecks finished one game back from first in the league. The offense might not wow opponents, but the defense and size can force teams to find a way to win in unorthodox ways, and that is what can give the Leathernecks a chance come conference play. item.title: Breaking down the Sox-Rox trade
item.description: Sean Sullivan is the x-factor in the most recent trade between the White Sox and Rockies. | ﻿(Photo by Norm Hall/Minor League Baseball via Getty Images) On November 19, the White Sox sent Luis Castillo and Davis Martin to the Colorado Rockies in exchange for left-handed pitching prospect Sean Sullivan and 17-year-old catcher Doug Veliz. Let’s break down the exchange and see what Chicago’s plans likely are. On a surface level, this is a better deal for the Rockies. Castillo is a veteran starting pitcher, with a 3.75 career ERA in 266 starts over the last decade. Martin is also an established starter, and 2026 was his career-best season for starts (28), innings pitched (146) and ERA (3.95). He spent the first half of the year as the ace of the White Sox staff, and finished with solid season-long numbers. Meanwhile, Sullivan was Colorado’s No. 10 prospect on MLB Pipeline’s 2025 rankings, making five major league starts in 2026 but was rocked to an 8.87 ERA. Veliz is a teenager whose total pro ball experience is 117 PAs in the Dominican Summer League. So, then, why would the White Sox trade two quality starting pitchers for two prospects, one of whom has already struggled in the big leagues and the other being about as inexperienced as you can get? Well, it’s pretty simple — the trade was a salary dump for Castillo. He’s entering his age-34 season, and struggled substantially in 2026. He had a 5.06 ERA for the Seattle Mariners when the White Sox acquired him at the trade deadline. He proceeded to be even worse for the Sox, posting an 8.42 ERA over six starts. Castillo finished the year with a 5.85 ERA, in 130 2/3 innings over 29 games (23 starts). He’s owed $22.75 million in 2027, with a vesting option for 2028, and was the most expensive player on the Sox payroll. Now, Castillo was much better in 2025 and had been very durable and productive up until 2026, so it’s possible he’ll bounce back next year. But the Sox probably don’t want a 34-year-old starter coming off a career-worst season to be their most expensive player. The Rockies have a track record for taking on aging, veteran pitchers, which made them a good candidate to take on Castillo’s salary. It’s much harder to figure out where Martin fits in. He pitched well for the Sox last year, and he’s not even arbitration-eligible until 2028. While the righthander had a solid 2026 (2.3 bWAR), he had a brutal stretch from June through August — which is a big chunk of the year. Martin was bad and/or hurt enough that he finished up in the bullpen. He also doesn’t have the most successful track record, only pitching partial seasons in 2022 and 2024 (never to great success), while missing most of 2023 to Tommy John surgery, and being lackluster in 2025. Martin owns a career ERA of 4.19 (with a league average 99 ERA+), having made 72 starts in parts of four seasons. item.title: The Grandson of The Greatest: Nico Ali Walsh on Fighting, Loss, and Protecting the Ali Boxing Reform Act
item.description: Nico Ali Walsh (center) testifies at a Senate Committee hearing on federal boxing laws in Washington, DC, April 2026. (Photo by Saul Loeb / AFP via Getty Images) “The nerves reach a peak right before the bell hits,” says Nico Ali Walsh , the bell signaling the suspension of assault laws. When it dings, he and another man are legally free to beat each other in the head and body as hard and fast as possible. It’s a family tradition. More from Spin: Zwan’s ‘Mary Star Of The Sea’ Gets Deluxe Vinyl Reissue Justin Timberlake Confronts His Legacy In Apple TV Doc Trailer Soundwalk Collective, Patti Smith Continue ‘Correspondences’ Nico’s granddad was, of course, the sweet science’s zenith—The Greatest!— Muhammad Ali . So, when a teenage Nico decided to try his hand in the ring, he had a very special oldtimer spurring him on. “We would always watch videos of my sparring,” says Nico. “Every time I didn’t want to keep going, he’d push me to keep going. He wanted me to keep fighting.” Nico was raised (and still lives) in Las Vegas, with Muhammad in the Phoenix area. “My first amateur fight was down the street from him [Ali]. He was sick at the time, so he didn’t make the fight,” says Nico. “The next day I went back to his house and said, ‘Poppy, I lost the fight.’ Then we had a conversation about how losing is an opportunity to come back even better. He motivated me,” says Nico, now 26 and fighting as a middleweight. The determined youngster turned pro at 21. Nico now has 17 pro fights, winning 13 and losing two, with a draw and a no contest. He fought the Thai boxer Kittisak Klinson last year in the Philippines’ iconic Araneta Coliseum, where, 50 years earlier, his grandfather and Joe Frazier fought the Thrilla in Manila. Nico Ali Walsh (at right) in the office with Billy Wagner, Madison Square Garden, 2022. (Photo by Williams Paul/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) Another fight he has picked up from his grandpa is the Muhammad Ali Boxing Reform Act . Championed by the Greatest himself, the Act protects boxers’ interests and independence and works against fixed contests, not allowing companies to simultaneously manage fighters, promote fights, and control the ranking and title system. Now, however, a new proposed law disingenuously titled Muhammad Ali American Boxing Revival Act is being pushed by Dana White, whose UFC juggernaut operates as an enclosed system in which fighters lack the independence of boxers. Dead opposite to what Muhammad Ali helped make law. “It’s absolutely horrible for boxing,” says Nico, “it will slash fighters’ rights by enveloping them in a monolithic corporation. I feel obligated to protect the sport of boxing.” Note: since this article went to press in SPIN’s beautiful, tactile, unmissable print edition, Nico dropped his opposition and now champions the Muhammed Ali American Boxing Revival Act in revised form, although many others remain opposed. item.title: Final Thoughts on Penguins Road Trip and Why It Matters
item.description: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect It was not an easy road trip. The Pittsburgh Penguins faced a pair of teams on back-to-back days with a combined 25 wins, and now 27. Fresh from the wreckage of continued unacceptable unraveling performances, the Penguins face swirling trade talk of an imminent nature and a playoff race replaced with trying to avoid being the worst team in hockey. While the Penguins lost both games in regulation, first to the Nashville Predators 4-3 and then to the Dallas Stars 1-0, the games marked improvement. The Penguins weren’t good against Nashville, but neither did they suffer their recent implosions. And Sunday, the Penguins were quite good and largely outplayed Dallas but couldn’tget that shot or the extra bounce past Dallas goalie Jake Oettinger. But the road trip served to show a few things within the Penguins team. First, and perhaps as important as anything else, the team has not quit on itself. There have been many, MANY teams facing the end who surrender to the situation and are lifeless, listless, and barely present. The Penguins are certainly not going that route. CROSBY They have more struggles ahead, but rallying for themselves was important. They can indeed play something akin to disciplined, professional hockey, and they have some talent, albeit not an overwhelming amount, especially without Evgeni Malkin in the lineup . Of course, their talent level is likely to drop after the trades begin, but the players have a chance to rescue some pride as well as up their trade values. **The second thing that matters is the competent play of the under-25 players. And that factor has a couple of benefits, not the least of which is the effect on the trade talks. In the Venn diagram of the trade bait players and the young players, there is an issue that overlaps. As the veterans submit better performances, their value goes up, but also general manager Kyle Dubas can breathe a little easier knowing the players arriving from Wilkes-Barre/Scranton can adequately fill spots and the situation will not fall apart. In fact, that might be the most important takeaway from the weekend. The situation shouldn’t become a dumpster fire if and when Dubas begins dealing. The losses put the Penguins in next-to-last in the NHL; they’re already losing with the veterans, so there is no incentive to keep this course. **The young players are clearly seizing their opportunity, but also still growing into the league. Coach Dan Muse elevated Avery Hayes to the second line Sunday. While too much shouldn’t be made of the move because the previous night’s inhabitant, Andrei Kuzmenko, had a couple of bad turnovers and again struggled to assert himself after a first-period goal, Hayes’s placement also signaled that the team was giving a young player a chance. After all, Hayes wouldn’t ordinarily be the first choice for second-line duty, even without Nick Robertson and Evgeni Malkin in the lineup. Also, the under-25 set has been playing well. Hendrix Lap

item.title: FIFA announces United States to cohost 2031 Women’s World Cup with Mexico, Jamaica, Costa Rica
item.description: Credit: Joseph Maiorana-Imagn Images The World Cup is returning to North America in short order. After a successful 2026 campaign for the men, FIFA has awarded the 2031 Women’s World Cup to the United States, Mexico, Jamaica, and Costa Rica, the tournament organizer announced on Monday. It will be the first time since 2003 that the U.S. will host the women’s event. Additionally, FIFA announced on Monday that the United Kingdom would host the 2035 tournament. Similar to the 2026 World Cup, the 2031 tournament is expected to be hosted primarily in the U.S., with select matches played in the other three countries. Per The Athletic , the U.S. is expected to host more than 80 of the 104 matches. Both the 2031 and 2035 tournaments were awarded without contest, meaning there were no other countries bidding to host the events. From a media standpoint, Netflix will be thrilled to have the 2031 tournament confirmed to take place primarily in the U.S. Netflix, of course, was awarded exclusive broadcast rights to the 2027 and 2031 World Cups back in 2024. And while the streamer was certainly counting on the 2031 event being hosted in the U.S., it is nice to finally have confirmation. If 2026 was any indication, a World Cup on home soil can drive considerable television audiences. This summer’s record-setting World Cup Final drew nearly 40 million viewers on Fox, shattering the prior record by more than double. Games featuring the United States also drew incredibly well, with the USMNT’s Round of 16 game against Belgium capturing 33 million viewers on Fox. And that’s only the English-language audience; Netflix will have both English- and Spanish-language rights in 2027 and 2031. News of the 2031 and 2035 Women’s World Cups being awarded comes as FIFA reviews bids for U.S. broadcasting rights to the 2030 men’s tournament, which are expected to attract at least $1.5 billion. Netflix is reportedly a frontrunner to land the rights, with Amazon’s Prime Video and a joint bid between Fox and Univision also in the running. item.description: Photo via Mega Agency Tyson Fury has fought some of the biggest battles of his career inside the boxing ring, but now he is opening up about a far more personal struggle, revealing a previously undisclosed schizophrenia diagnosis alongside his battle with bipolar disorder. The former heavyweight boxing champion, 38, discusses his struggles for the first time in the upcoming Netflix documentary Tyson Fury , premiering Friday, November 27, according to Deadline . The publication reports Tyson was diagnosed with schizophrenia following his 2015 victory over Wladimir Klitschko and later received a bipolar disorder diagnosis in 2017. “Words can’t explain the darkness I was in,” Tyson admitted in the documentary, per Deadline . “I came from the living version of the pits of hellfire, and I 100 percent thought at times I’d end up in a padded room with the door locked, and that scared me so much.” Photo via Mega Agency The boxer recalled struggling with overwhelming anxiety, particularly at night, before reaching a point where he felt unable to cope. “I was waking up in the night like this, the anxiety was crippling me. I just could not overcome it,” he explained. Eventually, Tyson sought help from a psychiatrist in London. “She asked me like a gazillion questions, and I ticked all the boxes, whatever was going on,” he recalled, listing “ depression, anxiety, bipolar disorder .” According to the National Institute of Mental Health, schizophrenia is a serious mental illness that affects how a person thinks, feels and behaves, sometimes causing hallucinations, delusions and difficulties with everyday functioning. Bipolar disorder is characterized by significant shifts in mood, energy and activity levels, including episodes of mania or hypomania and depression. The severity of Fury’s struggles became painfully clear on Halloween night in 2017, when he recalled feeling like “a fat mess, addicted to alcohol,” and realizing he could no longer cope on his own. His father, John Fury , also appears in the documentary, acknowledging that he had failed to recognize the seriousness of his son’s struggles. “Me being who I am and no understanding of anything, I didn’t want to see a depressed kid — and if I did see it, I paid no mind to it,” the 61-year-old admitted, according to Deadline . “But I understand now. It’s an illness, a terrible illness. I suffer with it myself,” John added. item.description: Cavan Sullivan named MLS Young Player of the Year 🌟 Philadelphia Union and USMNT midfielder Cavan Sullivan has capped a record-setting regular season by being named the 2026 MLS Young Player of the Year. In his first full campaign, the Man City-bound starlet emerged as one of the league's most exciting young talents, finishing with with a career-high 23 goal contributions (nine goals, 14 assists) in 29 appearances, and recorded a goal contribution in 10 consecutive matches, the longest such run by a teenager in MLS history. Both his total of 23 goal contributions and his 14 assists are the most ever by a teenager in a single MLS season. Sullivan's form also earned him MLS Player of the Month honors for September 2026. At 17 years and two days old, he became the youngest winner of the award in league history. His production on the club level soon translated to the international stage. Sullivan received his first call-up to the US men's national team in September and made his debut against Peru, becoming the second-youngest player in USMNT history to start a match. He has since collected four senior caps and added another milestone to his résumé by scoring against Mexico at 17 years and five days old, making him the youngest goalscorer in USMNT history.

item.title: How Columbus Crew turned it all around to set up MLS playoff showdown vs. Messi
item.description: It wasn’t working. Issa Tall had to admit that. Well, he didn’t really have to. The results told the story for him. The Columbus Crew didn’t win in its first five MLS matches. By the World Cup break, 15 games in, they’d only added two more. There needed to be changes, and they needed to be big. The Crew general manager moved quickly. In May, he fired coach Henrik Rydström, his first coaching hire as the Crew’s chief soccer officer, though he was quick to point out he was involved with previous hires including bringing in Wilfried Nancy. He spent big in the summer, revamping the Crew’s attack and adding pieces while bidding farewell to some regulars. Ten players arrived, and eight went out. It worked. The Crew turned the boat around, going from worst in the Eastern Conference to closing the season on a six-game win streak and having won eight of their last nine. That was enough not only to jump out of Thursday’s wild card match but to set up a First Round playoff series with Inter Miami, the reigning champion led by Lionel Messi. They also pushed to the U.S. Open Cup final, falling to St. Louis City in a penalty shootout. All of it led Tall to believe he made the right decisions, moving on quickly from the coach he thought was the right man for the job. “Some people could’ve waited the full year. Maybe it would’ve been safer, but that’s not me. That’s not us as a club. That’s not even the way we play!” Tall told USA TODAY Sports ahead of the playoffs. “You see how we are bold and are not afraid of taking risk. At the end of the day, it wasn’t even a risk necessarily. It was necessary for our players, for our club as a whole and I think ultimately we made the right decision to do it at that time.” Tall still stands by Rydström as a good coach, something he’s proving while leading Hammarby in Sweden which currently sits atop of the table after running off five consecutive wins. But he wasn’t the right fit for the Crew in the post-Nancy era. The Crew turned to Courtois, a former Crew academy and MLS Next Pro coach who continued the idea first expressed on the field so successfully by Nancy’s teams. The squad might not have been the entirely right squad, either. Tall turned to a scouting network led by Mark Nichols, bringing in a proven MLS veteran in Santi Rodriguez, Chile national team forward Gonzalo Tapia, securing a loan deal for Moroccan winger Anass Zaroury and signing designated player Brais Mendez, a Spanish attacker whose arrival from Real Sociedad brought to mind that of Cucho Hernandez. item.title: Beckham to be inducted into US Soccer Hall of Fame
item.description: David Beckham was knighted by King Charles in 2025 [Getty Images] David Beckham will be inducted into the United States' National Soccer Hall of Fame as part of its 2027 class. The former Manchester United and England midfielder, 51, made headlines in 2007 when he moved to Los Angeles from Spanish giants Real Madrid to join Major League Soccer (MLS) side LA Galaxy on a five-year contract. He made 124 appearances in all competitions for Galaxy, scoring 20 goals, and twice won both the MLS Cup and Supporters' Shield. Beckham's six seasons at Galaxy helped to raise the global profile of MLS and following his retirement in 2013, he became co-owner of MLS club Inter Miami, who signed Argentina World Cup winner Lionel Messi in 2023. His induction ceremony is set to take place on 16 April 2027 in Frisco, Texas. David Beckham's deal with LA Galaxy in 2007 was reportedly worth £128m [Getty Images] He was told the news he had been chosen on the veterans' ballot at an MLS board of governors' meeting on Thursday and said his time in the US has been "an incredible journey". Beckham, who had two loan spells with AC Milan in 2009 and 2010 while at Galaxy, added: "I'm looking to build this league and this sport in this great country for a long time." Meanwhile, former US internationals Megan Rapinoe and Julie Ertz have also been voted into the Hall of Fame in their first year of eligibility. Ballon d'Or winner Rapinoe, 41, and midfielder Ertz, 34, lifted the Women’s World Cup twice with with the US in 2015 and 2019. "To be alongside all the greatest players that have played for us, and played for our country alongside a bunch of my team-mates and friends, recognised like that in this way just means you were successful and a part of great teams," Rapinoe wrote on Instagram. item.title: NYCFC fires head coach Pascal Jansen after second-half collapse
item.description: NYCFC has fired head coach Pascal Jansen. New York City FC will be looking for a new head coach this offseason. Less than 24 hours after the club played its final match of the 2026 season, NYCFC announced that it fired head coach Pascal Jansen following a disappointing campaign that saw the club miss the playoffs for only the third time in its 12-year history. NYCFC went through an ugly 2026 season, finishing 11th in the Eastern Conference and being knocked out of playoff contention before the club even reached its Decision Day matchup with D.C. United on Saturday. The rough season was highlighted by the massive second-half collapse NYCFC went through following the World Cup break, posting a 5W-8D-6L record and sliding from eighth place to 11th. Jansen was informed of the decision by the club’s front office on Sunday morning and ultimately the decision to move on from him as head coach came down to the “failure of making playoffs” following a “disappointing season,” a source told The Post. item.title: Messi makes history with MLS Golden Boot
item.description: Messi retired from international football with Argentina earlier this year [Getty Images] Inter Miami forward Lionel Messi has become the first player in MLS history to win the Golden Boot in consecutive seasons. The eight-time Ballon d'Or winner scored 26 goals in 31 appearances, four clear of FC Dallas striker Peter Musa and five more than Nashville's English forward Sam Surridge. Messi becomes only the sixth player to land the award twice, joining a list that includes former Charlton Athletic and Southampton striker Bradley Wright-Phillips. In addition to his goals, the 39-year-old notched 17 assists over the course of the MLS season, ensuring his 43 goal contributions was also a league best for the second year in a row. And the World Cup winner could soon make more history as he bids to become the first three-time Landon Donovan MLS MVP winner. The former Argentina forward landed the award in 2024 as Inter Miami won the Supporters' Shield title and also in 2025 as they won the MLS Cup. Despite Messi's magic, Miami weren't able to land top spot in the MLS Eastern Conference, with the team finishing 17 points behind Surridge's Nashville. They will now face Columbus Crew over three games in the first round of the MLS Cup play-offs which begin later this month. item.title: On MLS Decision Day, D.C. United faces a familiar reality: Another season of failure
item.description: WASHINGTON — All around Major League Soccer , from Montreal to Miami and Seattle to San Diego, Saturday was Decision Day — the last act in an 8½-month production. While three playoff berths were in the balance, teams with guaranteed spots sought to improve their place. It's a day marked by desperation, scoreboard-watching and playoff-planning. At Audi Field, however, Decision Day felt more like Derision Day. For the seventh consecutive year, D.C. United, once a showpiece of a blossoming league, has no playoff plans — a near impossibility in a league that distributes postseason passes like a guy on a New York street corner handing out flyers for discount mattresses. Only Toronto FC's eight-year rut, starting with its 2007 expansion campaign, lasted longer. United wasn't even in the mix on Decision Day, its fate having been decided 10 days earlier. The lowly finale was against another failed side, New York City FC, which claimed a 1-0 victory on a late goal. While 2026 was an anomaly for the New Yorkers, it was the norm in the nation's capital. D.C. added another sad chapter to a rotten story under an ownership group, led by Jason Levien and Steve Kaplan, that has dragged the organization into irrelevance in not just the prospering league but in the local market and the ascending sport. The public-address announcer introduces the team as "your four-time MLS Cup champions," but he's been saying that for a long time. Given the league's evolution, it feels even longer. United's last title, in 2004, came in a 10-team operation — one-third the current landscape. Since then, 13 different clubs have hoisted the trophy. Less than two miles north of Audi Field, the U.S. Capitol witnessed a historic sea change Tuesday with a political wave that swept the ruling party out of office. Local soccer fans have had no such luck with those in power at Audi Field. Under the current regime … United hasn't won a playoff game in 11 years and hasn't advanced to the conference finals in 14. Twelve years have passed since it won at least half its 34 matches. United's only trophy in recent memory was the 2013 U.S. Open Cup, which came amid a horrific, three-win regular season. D.C. is on its fourth head coach since Ben Olsen's departure in late 2020 and its second head of soccer operations in four years. The current director, Erkut Sogut — an agent best known for representing former German star Mesut Özil — was hired last fall without any experience working for a team. Another goal conceded, another season to forget. Keisuke Kurokawa's frustration summed up D.C. United's latest disappointing chapter. Scott Taetsch via Getty Images United remains one of three MLS organizations without a developmental team bridging the youth academy to the first team. Efforts to build a complex in Baltimore for an MLS Next Pro operation have floundered. (Meanwhile, United's owners have launched a pro volleyball team.)
